title: Paul's Trial Before Felix

questions.question: The high priest Ananias came down to Caesarea with a spokesman named Tertullus to make accusations against Paul. What was Tertullus's opening accusation?
options: Paul was a plague, a creator of dissension among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes
Paul had defiled the temple by bringing Gentiles into the inner courts
Paul was an enemy of Caesar who taught people to reject Roman authority
Paul was a false prophet who led Jews away from the Law of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: Paul was a plague, a creator of dissension among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes
questions.explanation: Acts 24:5 (ESV): "For we have found this man a plague, one who stirs up riots among all the Jews throughout the world and is a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes."

questions.question: In his defense before Felix, Paul denied stirring up a crowd in the city. He said no more than how many days had passed since his arrival in Jerusalem?
options: Twelve days
Seven days
Twenty days
Forty days
questions.explanation: Acts 24:11 (ESV): "You can verify that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship in Jerusalem,"

questions.question: Paul described himself as a follower of the Way (which the accusers called a sect). He said he worshiped the God of his fathers, believing in everything "laid down by the Law and written in the..."?
options: Prophets
Scriptures
Torah
Book of Life
questions.explanation: Acts 24:14 (ESV): "But this I confess to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, I worship the God of our fathers, believing everything laid down by the Law and written in the Prophets,"

questions.question: Paul declared his hope: "that there will be a resurrection of both the just and the unjust." Because of this hope, he said he did what?
options: He always took pains to have a clear conscience toward both God and man
He kept all the customs of the Law of Moses diligently
He preached the gospel without ceasing wherever he traveled
He lived a life of fasting and prayer as witness to this truth
questions.correctAnswer: He always took pains to have a clear conscience toward both God and man
questions.explanation: Acts 24:16 (ESV): "So I always take pains to have a clear conscience toward both God and man."

questions.question: What had Paul actually come to Jerusalem to do at the time of his arrest, according to his defense?
options: To bring alms to his nation and to present offerings, having been ceremonially purified in the temple
To debate with the Sanhedrin about the resurrection of the dead
To visit James and the Jerusalem church with news of his missions
To observe the Passover feast as required by the Jewish law
questions.correctAnswer: To bring alms to his nation and to present offerings, having been ceremonially purified in the temple
questions.explanation: Acts 24:17-18 (ESV): "Now after several years I came to bring alms to my nation and to present offerings. While I was doing this, they found me purified in the temple..."

questions.question: Felix already had a fairly accurate knowledge of the Way. He deferred the case, saying he would decide when Lysias the tribune came down. Where did he keep Paul in the meantime?
options: In custody but with some liberty, allowing his friends to care for his needs
In the common prison of Caesarea until Lysias arrived
Under house arrest in a private Christian home
Under guard at Herod's palace with full personal freedom
questions.correctAnswer: In custody but with some liberty, allowing his friends to care for his needs
questions.explanation: Acts 24:23 (ESV): "Then he gave orders to the centurion that he should be kept in custody but have some liberty, and that none of his friends should be prevented from attending to his needs."

questions.question: Felix sent for Paul and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus. What topics caused Felix to be alarmed?
options: Righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment
The resurrection of the dead and the wrath of God
The suffering of Christ and the requirement for repentance
The kingdom of God and the authority of Christ over Caesar
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment
questions.explanation: Acts 24:25 (ESV): "And as he reasoned about righteousness and self-control and the coming judgment, Felix was alarmed and said, 'Go away for the present....'"

questions.question: Why did Felix continue to send for Paul and have conversations with him?
options: He was hoping that money would be given him by Paul
He was genuinely interested in learning more about the Way
He wanted to release Paul but feared the Jewish leaders
He was ordered by Rome to investigate the Christian movement
questions.correctAnswer: He was hoping that money would be given him by Paul
questions.explanation: Acts 24:26 (ESV): "At the same time he hoped that money would be given him by Paul. So he sent for him often and conversed with him."

questions.question: For how long did Felix keep Paul in custody before being succeeded by Porcius Festus?
options: Two years
One year
Three years
Six months
questions.explanation: Acts 24:27 (ESV): "When two years had elapsed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And desiring to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison."

questions.question: Why did Felix leave Paul in prison when he was succeeded by Festus?
options: Desiring to do the Jews a favor
Because Paul had not yet been formally tried
Because Festus had not yet reviewed the case
Because Paul had refused to deny being a Christian
questions.correctAnswer: Desiring to do the Jews a favor
questions.explanation: Acts 24:27 (ESV): "And desiring to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison."

questions.question: Tertullus accused Paul of trying to profane the temple. Who had seized Paul in the temple, and what did Paul say about their presence at the trial?
options: Jews from Asia had seized him; they ought to be present before Felix to make their accusation if they had anything against him
The temple guard had arrested him; they should testify about what they saw
Ananias himself had given the order; he should substantiate his charge
Roman soldiers had seized him; their report should be read before Felix
questions.correctAnswer: Jews from Asia had seized Paul; they ought to be present before Felix to make their accusation if they had anything against him
questions.explanation: Acts 24:18-19 (ESV): "...some Jews from Asia—who ought to be here before you and to make an accusation, should they have anything against me."

questions.question: Felix told Paul to go away for the present and said he would "summon you when I get an opportunity." What was Felix's ongoing spiritual state?
options: He was alarmed during Paul's reasoning but never responded in repentance
He was convicted briefly but hardened his heart and refused further meetings
He privately converted to Christ but hid it for political reasons
He remained philosophically curious but saw no personal need for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: He was alarmed during Paul's reasoning but never responded in repentance
questions.explanation: Acts 24:25-27 (ESV): Felix was alarmed but sent Paul away, and continued to converse with him while hoping for a bribe, never committing to the faith.

questions.question: Paul admitted to believing in "the Way" but insisted it was not a sect contrary to the Law. He said the only thing the council could convict him of crying out was about what single issue?
options: "With respect to the resurrection of the dead I am on trial before you this day."
"It is about the hope of Israel that I am being judged."
"I stand here on trial because of the gospel of Jesus Christ."
"I am judged for my witness to the Gentiles about our God."
questions.correctAnswer: "With respect to the resurrection of the dead I am on trial before you this day."
questions.explanation: Acts 24:21 (ESV): "other than this one thing that I cried out while standing among them: 'It is with respect to the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you this day.'"

questions.question: Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess, to hear Paul speak about faith in Christ Jesus. Who was Drusilla?
options: The wife of Felix and a Jewess
A daughter of Herod Agrippa who had become Felix's consort
A Gentile woman who had converted to Judaism
A Roman noblewoman fascinated by Jewish religion
questions.correctAnswer: The wife of Felix and a Jewess
questions.explanation: Acts 24:24 (ESV): "After some days Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, and he sent for Paul and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus."

questions.question: The Jews who came from Jerusalem had a spokesman before Felix. What does his name Tertullus suggest about him?
options: He was a professional Roman-style orator (the name is Latin, indicating he was likely a hired Roman lawyer)
He was a Pharisee trained in Roman rhetoric in Alexandria
He was a Levite serving as official spokesman for the high priest
He was a Greek convert to Judaism skilled in Hellenistic debate
questions.correctAnswer: He was a professional Roman-style orator (the name is Latin, indicating he was likely a hired Roman lawyer)
questions.explanation: Acts 24:1 (ESV): "...with a spokesman named Tertullus." The Latin name and eloquent opening speech suggest he was a hired Roman advocate.

key_verse_text: So I always take pains to have a clear conscience toward both God and man.
